findings.title: The fix does not make injection impossible: the heredoc delimiter PLANNER_DRAFT_PATH_EOF_9f3b6a2d1e8c4caa is checked into the tracked agent prompt, so a payload containing a line matching it verbatim still terminates the heredoc early, before Python's check runs.
findings.evidence: agent-workflows/idea-planner-agent.md:141-147, .claude/agents/idea-planner.md. Reproduced live: a path payload containing the delimiter line followed by `touch .../PWNED_MARKER` executed the touch as a shell command (marker file created) while Python saw only the truncated first line (FileNotFoundError); re.fullmatch() never ran. test/test_planner_safe_write.py:364-378 only checks properties of the delimiter string and documents the gap as an accepted limit; no test feeds the token through the real command.
findings.consequence: Injection remains possible for anyone who reads the repository; the prose claim that the delimiter is unguessable is false.
findings.minimal_fix: Stop passing the path through a shell heredoc at all: the agent writes the path to a fixed scratch file with its file-write tool (not bash) and the Python command open()s that file directly.

Its "Minor" paragraph lists checks that held (regex matches codes.py COUNTER including child codes; tests fail on the pre-fix form; generated file current) and is not recorded as findings. SM observation, not a change to the finding: the agent definition's tools line is `Read, Grep, Bash`, yet its "How you write the draft" section tells it to write the draft "with your file-write tool"; without a Write tool the draft content itself would also pass through Bash.
